newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan allows insurers to invest in HK securities.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan allows insurers to invest in HK securities.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Tuesday it had revised rules to allow domestic insurance companies to invest in foreign securities, including Hong Kong's, but investment in China was still banned.
The announcement, which became effective immediately, came after Hong Kong's handover to China at midnight on June 30.
The ministry also raised domestic insurers' foreign investment ceiling to 10 percent of total insurance funds, up from the previous five percent, it said in a statement.

The Economic Daily News said on Tuesday that insurance funds are now totalled at T$1.2 trillion and the new move would mean that an additional T$60 billion of such funds would be allowed to invest in foreign securities.
Previously, local insurers were only allowed to invest in 20 foreign stock markets, including the New York stock exchange, the ministry statement said.
Foreign securities included all securities traded in overseas main exchanges and over-the-counter exchanges, the statement added.
Under the new rules, local insurers are allowed to invest in foreign insurance companies, as well as in foreign floating rate notes or other securities papers approved by the ministry, it said.
